## Why This Is Asked

Tests integration of policy-as-code, attestation, and runtime security across a multi-tenant cluster. Candidates must show how to bind OPA, Kyverno, Rekor/cosign, and Falco to a coherent workflow, plus a concrete verification plan.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance and attestations (cosign, Rekor)
- Policy-as-code (OPA, Kyverno)
- Runtime security (Falco/eBPF)
- Multi-tenant governance and testability

## Code Example

```javascript
// OPA Rego (conceptual)
package kubernetes.admission
violation[reason] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
  not imageIsAttested(image)
  reason = "image provenance missing"
}
```

```javascript
// Kyverno policy (conceptual)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-provenance-and-security
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-nonroot
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "must set runAsNonRoot and readOnlyRootFilesystem"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              runAsNonRoot: true
  - name: require-attested-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "image must have Rekor cosign attestation"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - image: "*attested*"
```

```javascript
// Falco rule (conceptual)
- rule: Unsigned Image Usage
  condition: container.image.signature == ""
  output: "Unsigned image detected: %container.image.repository"
  priority: WARN
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle attestation key rotation?
- How would you measure false positives and performance impact?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy design, RBAC scoping, and CI integration for a high-sensitivity platform.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- RBAC bindings (RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding)
- Namespace-scoped allowlists and auditing in CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (RBACWhitelist)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: rbacwhitelist
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package rbacwhitelist
      violation[{msg}] {
        binding := input.review.object
        binding.kind == \"RoleBinding\" or binding.kind == \"ClusterRoleBinding\"
        role := binding.roleRef.name
        ns := binding.metadata.namespace
        allowed := data.allowlist[ns]
        role != \"\"; role notin allowed
        msg := sprintf(\"RBAC violation: %s bound to %s in %s\", [binding.kind, role, ns])
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (per-namespace allowlist)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RbacWhitelist
metadata:
  name: rbac-whitelist-prod
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [\"rbac.authorization.k8s.io\"]
      kinds: [\"RoleBinding\", \"ClusterRoleBinding\"]
  parameters:
    namespaceAllowlists:
      production: [\"view\", \"edit\"]
      staging: [\"view\"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this with CI/CD and simulate violations?
- How would you handle dynamic/temporary permissions without conflicting with the allowlist?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design production-grade policy gates that enforce artifact provenance and data lineage—critical concerns in multi-cloud ML deployments where governance and compliance are paramount. The question tests practical experience with cryptographic attestation, policy-as-code frameworks, and CI/CD pipeline design.

## Sample OPA Policy

```rego
package data.provenance

default allow = false

allow {
    input.review.kind == "Deployment"
    some i
    input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].image
    startswith(image, input.config.trusted_registry)
    verify_signature(image)
    tenant_allowed(input.review.namespace)
    lineage_tag_valid(image)
}

verify_signature(image) {
    not missing_signature(image)
    crypto.verify(input.artifacts[image].sig, input.artifacts[image].digest, input.config.public_key)
}

missing_signature(image) {
    not input.artifacts[image]
}

tenant_allowed(ns) {
    input.config.tenant_allowlist[ns]
}

lineage_tag_valid(image) {
    tag := input.artifacts[image].lineage_tag
    input.catalog.tags[tag]
}
```

## Sample Kyverno Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-artifact-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: validate-signed-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: '{{ request.namespace }}'
        operator: In
        value: '{{ tenantAllowlist }}'
    validate:
      message: "Artifact must be signed and from trusted registry"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '{{ trustedRegistry }}@*'
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        preconditions:
          all:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotIn
            value: [""]
        context:
        - name: artifactData
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/artifacts/{{ element.image | split("@")[1] }}"
        - name: signatureValid
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/verify/{{ artifactData.digest }}"
            statement: "$.signature.valid == true"
```

## Failing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-inference
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        image: untrusted-registry.com/models:v1.0  # ❌ Not in trusted registry
        env:
        - name: ARTIFACT_DIGEST
          value: "sha256:abc123"
        - name: LINEAGE_TAG
          value: "raw-data-v2"  # ❌ Tag not in data catalog
```

**Failure Reasons:**
1. Image not from trusted registry
2. Lineage tag `raw-data-v2` not registered in data catalog
3. Missing cryptographic signature
4. Tenant `tenant-a` not in allowlist

## Passing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-inference
  namespace: tenant-a
  annotations:
    artifact.provenance/digest: "sha256:def456"
    artifact.provenance/signature: "LS0tLS1..."
    artifact.provenance/tenant: "tenant-a"
    artifact.provenance/lineage: "processed-features-v1"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        image: trusted-registry.com/tenant-a/models:v2.1@sha256:def456  # ✓ Trusted registry
        env:
        - name: ARTIFACT_DIGEST
          value: "sha256:def456"
        - name: LINEAGE_TAG
          value: "processed-features-v1"  # ✓ Tag exists in catalog
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. **Extract artifact reference** from deployment manifest
2. **Fetch artifact metadata** from trusted registry API
3. **Validate cryptographic signature** against registry's public key
4. **Verify tenant allowlist** — confirm namespace exists in per-tenant policy
5. **Check data catalog** — confirm lineage tag is registered and active
6. **Attest result** — write provenance record to audit log with timestamp and CI run ID
7. **Block or permit** pipeline execution based on policy evaluation

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This task tests practical CI gating for container hygiene: linting with Hadolint and enforcing image tagging discipline across manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Hadolint integration in GitHub Actions
- YAML parsing to inspect image tags
- Regular expressions for pinning (no latest, no -dev) and clear failure messages
- Practical debugging of lint vs. policy failures

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci-docker-k8s.yml
name: CI Gate: Dockerfile lint + tag pin
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ '**' ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@v3
        with:
          dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
      - name: Check pinned image tags
        run: |
          set -e
          if grep -RIn 'image:.*:.*(latest|dev.*)' manifests || true; then
            echo 'Unpinned image tag detected' ; exit 1;
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale this gate to many repos?
- How would you extend checks for other tag policies (sha256 digests)?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic manifest validation, API version awareness, and simple, repeatable CI gating for multi-service apps.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes manifests, apiVersion, kind
- Labels discipline (app, version)
- Image digests and internal registries
- Lightweight CI gates (GitHub Actions) and script-based checks

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in $(git ls-files '*.yaml' '*.yml'); do
  api=$(yq e '.apiVersion' "$f")
  if [[ "$api" == "apps/v1beta1" || "$api" == "extensions/v1beta1" ]]; then
    echo "Deprecated apiVersion: $api in $f"; exit 1
  fi
  if ! yq e 'has(.metadata.labels.app) and has(.metadata.labels.version)' "$f" >/dev/null; then
    echo "Missing labels in $f"; exit 1
  fi
  if ! yq e '.spec.template.spec.containers[].image' "$f" | grep -q '@sha256'; then
    echo "Image must use digest in $f"; exit 1
  fi
done
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (deprecated API, missing labels)
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: internal-registry.example.com/app/web:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (apps/v1, labels, image digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example
  labels:
    app: web
    version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
        version: v1
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: internal-registry.example.com/app/web@sha256:deadbeef...
```

## Why This Is Asked

This evaluates the ability to translate security requirements into automated validation for Helm-rendered Kubernetes manifests, demonstrating practical DevOps security implementation skills.

## Key Concepts

- Helm template rendering for manifest generation
- Kubernetes container securityContext enforcement
- GitHub Actions as CI/CD security gates
- Lightweight YAML validation using shell scripting

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Helm Security Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'charts/**'
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-helm@v3
      - name: Render and validate security context
        run: |
          helm template myapp charts/myapp > rendered.yaml
          # Validate security context fields
          python3 scripts/validate-security.py rendered.yaml
```

```python
# scripts/validate-security.py
import sys, yaml
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
for doc in docs:
    if doc.get('kind') == 'Deployment':
        for container in doc['spec']['template']['spec']['containers']:
            ctx = container.get('securityContext', {})
            if not ctx.get('runAsNonRoot'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing runAsNonRoot")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('runAsUser', 0) >= 1000:
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} runAsUser < 1000")
                sys.exit(1)
            if not ctx.get('readOnlyRootFilesystem'):
                print(f"FAIL: {container['name']} missing readOnlyRootFilesystem")
                sys.exit(1)
print("All security context checks passed")
```

```yaml
# Failing Helm template - missing readOnlyRootFilesystem
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          # readOnlyRootFilesystem: true  # Missing - will fail CI
```

```yaml
# Passing Helm template - complete security context
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

## Verification

**Local testing:**
```bash
helm template myapp charts/myapp | python3 scripts/validate-security.py -
```

**CI verification:** The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests, rendering templates and validating security context fields before allowing merge.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly
